clue.text: Smartest form of bedding

indicators.note: a new form of the word Smartest means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A boast that some bedding is the cleverest kind around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'form of' tells you to rearrange the letters of SMARTEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A padded mattress is the main item of bedding on which a sleeper lies.

clue.text: A moving proposal

explanation.surface: A proposal that stirs the emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like an adjective meaning touching, but 'A moving' is a noun phrase: an act of movement.
explanation.definitionFit: Movement is the physical sense; a formal suggestion put to a meeting for debate is the other.

clue.text: Features an artist surrounded by birds

indicators.note: the artist is placed inside, with the birds on either side

parts.note: tits are small songbirds
RA, Royal Academician, is the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painting's features show an artist in a flock of birds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrounded by' is the container signal; RA (Royal Academician) is the standard crossword artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Traits are distinguishing characteristics, a synonym of features in the sense of qualities.

clue.text: Report concerning queue forming

parts.note: re is the formal word for about or concerning
a tail is a line of people waiting, a queue

explanation.surface: News of a queue building up outside somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To retail a story is to recount or relate it, an older sense of passing on news.

clue.text: Concealing failed M.O.T.,he grins

indicators.note: a failed version of the phrase has its letters jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A motorist hides a failed vehicle test result behind a grin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' is the signal to rearrange MOTHEGRINS. An MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for cars.
explanation.definitionFit: To smother something is to cover it up or suppress it, a synonym of hiding.

clue.text: The German grabs a pub meal

indicators.note: the German word takes hold of the pub, holding it inside

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
an inn is a pub

explanation.surface: A German grabs a quick meal at the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabs' is the container signal: the German article takes hold of the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Dinner is the main meal of the day.

clue.text: Bad spirit allowed, that's understood

parts.note: an imp is a small mischievous devil
licit means lawful or permitted

explanation.surface: It goes without saying that a wicked ghost is permitted.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is implied rather than stated, so taken as understood without words.

clue.text: A number of bonds are for a ten-year period

parts.note: nine is one example of a number
ties are bonds or links between people

explanation.surface: Financial bonds being issued for a decade-long term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bonds' suggests finance, but here they are ties of connection.
explanation.definitionFit: The nineties are the decade from '90 to '99, a span of ten years.

clue.text: Uneasy, so maybe steer around left with some craft

indicators.note: the letters built so far go around the single letter for left
maybe signals the word steer is not as written but in some other arrangement

parts.note: taken as written before rearranging
SS stands for steamships, so more than one craft

explanation.surface: A nervous sailor steers to port and around other boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'so maybe' rearranges the steering word into RESTE; 'around' then wraps the built letters about the abbreviation for left. 'some craft' means several ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless describes someone fidgety and unable to settle, much like anxious.

clue.text: Tot in car settling down and drawing

indicators.note: a fidgeting child settling down shifts position, so the letters move into a new order

explanation.surface: A toddler in the back of the car finally settles and starts to draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'settling down' signals an anagram of TOTINCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Traction is the act of pulling a load, and drawing also means pulling.

clue.text: Fancies there's nothing to secure bearings

parts.note: O, the shape of zero, means nothing
to pin something is to fasten it
E and S are compass bearings, east and south

explanation.surface: A dreamer imagines nothing is holding their direction steady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bearings' are compass points, here E (east) and S (south).
explanation.definitionFit: To opine is to hold or express a view, as one thinks or reckons something.

clue.text: Sweeping victory for Labour?

explanation.surface: A landslide election win for Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as OUT RIGHT: a Labour win puts the Right (the Conservatives) out. Labour is Britain's main left-wing party.
explanation.definitionFit: Sweeping means complete or total; the other sense is the political Right being ousted from power.

clue.text: The boastful character out of step is told off

indicators.note: the name is taken out of a run of consecutive letters across these words

explanation.surface: A braggart who marches out of time is given a dressing-down.
explanation.walkthrough: Pistol is the swaggering soldier in Shakespeare's Henry plays and The Merry Wives of Windsor; he sits inside 'steP IS TOLd'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Ancient Pistol is the stock braggart, a loud boaster in Falstaff's circle.

clue.text: Cut the string and share out fairly

parts.note: a lace is a cord or string, as in a shoelace
to ration is to divide a supply into fair portions

explanation.surface: Instructions to cut a length of string and divide it evenly.
explanation.definitionFit: A laceration is a jagged wound, a tear in the skin.

clue.text: They'll arrange for alternative singers-a mistake

parts.note: or is the word that introduces an alternative

indicators.note: a mistaken copy of the words gets their letters in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Choirmasters arrange things to stop singers making errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistake' is the anagram signal; the singers-a letters become GANISERS, with the word for an alternative in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisers are the people who plan and set up events, ordering things.

clue.text: Put round about shortage resulting in power failure

indicators.note: the round is placed about, on either side of, the shortage

parts.note: a bout is a round of boxing or fighting
lack means want or shortage

explanation.surface: An electricity shortage leads to the lights going out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put' just instructs the solver; 'about' is the container signal, and 'round' is a boxing round, not a shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a cut in the electricity supply leaving everything dark.

clue.text: Delinquent wanting a tip in advance

indicators.note: the tip is put in the middle of the advance

parts.note: to advance an idea is to offer it, and an offer is an advance
the end of something is its tip

explanation.surface: A young criminal who is short of a gratuity paid up front.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tip' suggests a gratuity, but here it is an end, as in the tip of a finger.
explanation.definitionFit: A delinquent is a lawbreaker, especially a young one, someone who commits crimes.

clue.text: Whip-it's doubtfully accepted by the hunt

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are taken inside the hunt

parts.note: a chase is a hunt

indicators.note: doubtfully suggests the word is uncertain in form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Debate over whether whipping is tolerated by fox hunters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubtfully' rearranges the letters to TIS, which 'accepted by' places inside the hunting word.
explanation.definitionFit: To chastise is to punish or scold severely, as with a beating.

clue.text: A sinister blow!

explanation.surface: An ominous punch lands.
explanation.walkthrough: Sinister is Latin for left, so 'A sinister' is a person who favours that hand; a blow struck with that hand is the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A southpaw person is the first sense; a punch thrown from the weaker side is the second.

clue.text: The father is about fifty and a manual worker

indicators.note: the father goes about the number, which sits inside

parts.note: pater is Latin and old public-school slang for father
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A dad nearing fifty who works with his hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is about' puts L inside PATER.
explanation.definitionFit: A plater is a tradesman who coats or fits metal plates, a skilled craftsman's job.

clue.text: Stick-up in a ruin of ancient Greece

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rod is a stick

indicators.note: to ruin the words is to wreck their order

explanation.surface: A robbery staged in some crumbling Greek ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick-up' looks like a robbery: 'up' turns ROD into DOR, and 'ruin' rearranges IN A to IAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dorians were one of the Hellenic peoples, so Dorian means belonging to them.

clue.text: To part with a note is almost unbearable

parts.note: to part things is to cut them apart, to sever
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: Leaving a farewell message proves nearly too much to bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Severe pain or strain is extreme and hard to endure.

clue.text: Fold when troops go into action

indicators.note: the troops enter the action, placed inside it

parts.note: a case is a legal action or lawsuit
RE, the Royal Engineers, are British army troops

explanation.surface: An army unit gives way when soldiers are sent into battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' looks military but is a lawsuit; 'go into' is the container signal, with RE (Royal Engineers) as the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: A crease is a line made by folding, as in paper or cloth.

clue.text: Muse or manage quite well without all one

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the words go around the others

parts.note: to cope is to get by adequately
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A poet who gets by fine even when left entirely alone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, so the coping word goes around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Calliope is the Greek goddess of epic poetry, one of the nine Muses.

clue.text: Lay down frock

explanation.surface: Instructions to put a dress down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frock' looks like a dress, but as a verb it means to give a priest's habit, making a clergyman.
explanation.definitionFit: To decree or enact is the first sense; to invest someone as a priest is the second.

clue.text: Help retired people and get only abuse

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn or drawn back, so the word for help is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help
a tribe is a people or community

explanation.surface: Charity workers who give help find only insults in return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retired' (drawn back) turns the helping word round to give DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A diatribe is a bitter verbal attack, a tirade of insults.

clue.text: New trader in the black

indicators.note: a new version of the word trader has its letters in a fresh order

explanation.surface: A fresh trader is already making a profit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the black' looks like being in profit, but means coated with black tar.
explanation.definitionFit: Tarred means coated with tar, a thick dark pitch, so blackened.

clue.text: Break popular with those on edge

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the fringe is the outer edge, or those at the margins of a group

explanation.surface: A trendy group mixing with anxious outsiders breaks the rules.
explanation.definitionFit: To infringe a rule is to violate or breach it.
